answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit bids, then weight voting power by stake rather than by account count. Splitting one deposit across a hundred fake agents creates no extra influence, while misconduct—such as double-signing a transaction—can forfeit the bond. This does not stop every attack: an adversary can buy more stake, but must risk real capital for the duration of the voyage. A cipher-verified claim may help link actions, yet the inlet is the costly bond, not the number of names.
